hypothesis: An explicitly measured visual-first trial can test whether earlier visual rejection improves useful iteration without weakening integrity checks.
reason: Bounded documentation change preserves integrity gates and requires a prospective worth-it decision.

supportingEvidence.claim: Declares matched visual evidence, total effort, unknowns and a mandatory post-iteration verdict.

contraryEvidence.claim: Earlier single-view discrimination still incurred review overruns; ordering alone may not reduce cost.

unknowns: Comparable historical cost measurements are unavailable.
Deferred integrity checks may expose expensive defects.

prediction.ifTrue: The next art iteration discriminates visual value earlier while retaining required integrity checks.
prediction.ifFalse: Review overhead or late defects consume any benefit.

test.action: Update workflow and diagram; require the next art phase review to record retain, modify, reject or inconclusive before another art phase.
test.success: Matched visual comparison and full-cost evidence support a provisional decision; missing comparability remains explicit.
test.failure: Documentation implies proven efficiency, bypasses integrity, or permits advancement without the verdict.
